In Java development, Spring programming is multi-faceted in a class of its own. The framework helped popularize such important Java development practices as dependency injection and inversion of control (IoC). Combined with JavaScript on the front-end, the framework shines when you hire full stack developer teams to develop complete solutions. Both developers and large enterprises like Spring web development, for different, but overlapping reasons. Let’s find out how you can hire dedicated Java developer with the knowledge of Spring framework.

Spring Developer for Hire Popularity

For backend developers, the framework offers the following set of popular features:

  • Easy integration – The framework is compatible with major Java technologies such as JDBC, Hibernate, and others. It works with a wide range of databases and middleware, including Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, MongoDB, and others.
  • Aspect-oriented programming – Programming with aspects is a different way of programming thinking that involves isolating cross-cutting functionality into distinct “aspects.” Rather than have code repeated throughout your application to handle these aspects each time they are needed, with aspect-oriented programming (AOP), you can reuse aspects. Applying them to handle functionality becomes a simple issue of using annotations to invoke the aspect logic.
  • Testing support – The framework has excellent testing support. You can use it with tools like JUnit as well as mocking utilities such as Mockito. This makes the framework a fit for cutting edge development methodologies such as Test Driven Development (TDD) and Behavior Driven Development (BDD). When done right, testing can improve the integrity of your entire code base. Your applications will run more smoothly and contain fewer bugs.
  • MVC web development – For the web, the framework makes use of a Model-View-Controller programming paradigm. This splits up web development cleanly into three distinct areas that make designing and developing web applications much easier. The result is more robust web applications that are simpler to develop.

A survey by DZone revealed that Spring is among the top 2 Java frameworks, neck and neck with JSF (Java Server Faces).

The popularity of Spring Versus Other Java Web Frameworks

Why to Hire Java Spring Developer for Backend Development

When it comes to the capabilities of the framework, enterprises like the following features:

  • Core Java – The framework enables development using core Java, both the language and its related technologies. The complexities of using a proprietary Java extension by Spring developer are taken away.
  • Talent availability – The popularity of the framework among large companies has encouraged many Spring developers to invest the time necessary to learn the framework. This effect is self-reinforcing: as the framework becomes more popular with Spring developers, more companies see it as a safe bet for finding the talent necessary to develop their applications.
  • Open Source – The flexible open-source nature of the framework makes it a cost-effective enterprise solution, but the advantages of open source are much more than that. Open source development enables any highly skilled Spring team both to extend the core Spring framework as well as leverage others’ customizations. The rate of code-sharing and technology iteration is higher since the framework has numerous contributors making open source contributions. With so many committed stakeholders, long term vibrancy of the Spring source code is all but assured.
  • Compatibility with enterprise technology – The compatibility of the framework with other tools in the Java ecosystem makes it easier for businesses to pair it with their existing tools or technology stacks. This eases the adoption of Spring web development for any large business with an existing tech infrastructure of considerable size.

Alternatives to Spring Software Development

The alternatives to this framework include JavaEE, Struts, Vaadin, JSF, Grails, and Play. The key to realize is that Spring takes a very modular approach. What this means is that any Spring web developer is not tied to using a particular module if he does not want to. He can easily swap out a Spring module with another Java module. This means that you can essentially use the framework alongside another framework that would normally be regarded as a competitor of Spring. For example, at the web layer, there are many alternative frameworks available that you could use to replace Spring MVC, the web framework that handles web functionality in the default stack. Your options for this replacement include:

  • Tapestry
  • Velocity
  • Struts
  • JSF

There are numerous options that can be tied into the core Spring configuration in place of SpringMVC. The result is that the core framework will accommodate any shifts in technology preference that your team may have as you go about designing your Java solutions.

Spring Application Development Advantages and Disadvantages

As the table of pros and cons above shows, Spring’s considerable complexity creates a situation in which you want the very best Spring developers available. This is because the framework is a very powerful one while, at the same time, it has a steep learning curve. Any junior Spring developer can quickly become productive, but it takes years and multiple Spring deployments to really sort out the problematic areas where developers tend to get things wrong. To ensure your application backend is developed with the most robust standards, you will need to hire Spring developer with deep professional experience.
